title: EU General Affairs Council: MFF 2028-34 Debate, Rule of Law Reviews, Electoral Rights Adopted
detail: The EU General Affairs Council (GAC) met in Brussels on May 26 to prepare the June 18-19 European Council agenda and advance several legislative items. Ministers held a substantive policy debate on the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) 2028-2034, including the proposed European Competitiveness Fund and National Partnership Plans — the most significant EU budget negotiation since the 2021-2027 MFF. The Council received an update on EU-UK relations, covering ongoing negotiations on a veterinary/SPS agreement, ETS linkage, and the Youth Experience Scheme following the May 2025 EU-UK Summit. The GAC also held rule of law country-specific dialogues on France, Croatia, Italy, and Latvia, and received a separate Article 7(1) update on Hungary. The Council formally adopted a directive strengthening EU citizens' municipal voting rights in other member states, and proxy voting amendments enabling MEPs to vote during pregnancy and early parenthood.

title: Ukraine's Cluster 1 EU Accession Vote Delayed to June 16 — All Six Clusters Targeted for One Month
detail: Despite earlier expectations, no formal vote was held on May 26 to open Cluster 1 ('Fundamentals') of Ukraine's EU accession negotiations. Ukraine's Deputy PM Taras Kachka publicly called for all six negotiating clusters to be opened by June, stating that Ukraine is 'already behind the deadline' for the fastest accession process in EU history. Croatia's EU minister reaffirmed Croatia's position that Ukraine is 'more than ready' to open the first cluster and backed a June timeline. A concrete schedule emerged: the European Commission will formally propose opening Cluster 1 at the General Affairs Council on June 16, 2026, with EU leaders expected to endorse this at the European Council on June 18-19. Hungary's new Foreign Minister signalled Budapest 'will not block anything,' removing the last political veto obstacle from the Orbán era.

title: EU Agriculture Council: €400M Fertiliser Action Plan to Address European Farming Crisis
detail: The EU Agriculture and Fisheries Council met on May 26 to address the European fertiliser affordability and availability crisis. The European Commission unveiled an action plan featuring approximately €400 million in targeted aid for farmers, CAP flexibility measures allowing member states to redirect rural development funds, and strategic autonomy measures to reduce EU agricultural dependency on imported nitrogen and potash fertilisers — supply chains disrupted by Russia's war in Ukraine and the subsequent sanctions regime. Ministers also exchanged views on EU agri-food trade with third countries, including concerns about WTO-compatibility of proposed 'mirror clauses' on food safety standards for imports.
